summary: Lewis Doney is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Brandon Dotson, and Sam van Schaik, and held posts at LMU Munich (circa 2013-2019) and University of Bonn (circa 2021).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson, Alex Wayman, and Minoru Kiyota. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (circa 1967-2002), becoming Emeritus.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983-1991) and secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991-2000). In 2000, he became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center.
Liang Cai works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas from circa 2007 to 2011.

Lili Zheng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (circa 2008-2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, with Kuan Wu and Kuo-wei Liu serving as committee members.

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, earned her PhD at SOAS (circa 1996-2001), and became Curator of the Central Asian Collection at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst circa 2007.

Lin Heng is an Indologist who completed an MA at Silpakorn University (circa 2012-2015) under Chainarong Klinnoi, with Chirapat Prapandvidya, Sombat Mangmeesukhsiri, Samniang Leurmsai, Bumroong Kham-Ek, and C. Panduranga Bhatta serving on the committee.

Linda Jean LaMacchia works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe, along with committee members Kirin Narayan, John D. Dunne, Joseph W. Elder, and Frank Salomon.

Linda Learman is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral studies under Robert P. Weller (circa 1994-2001) and was mentored by Peter N. Gregory as a postdoctoral researcher.
Linda Penkower is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993. She has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Florida State University (circa 2005-2007) supervised by Bryan J. Cuevas, with Kathleen M. Erndl, John Corrigan, and Martin Kavka as committee members and teachers.
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who completed her PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo in 2014.

Lionel David Barnett was an Indologist educated at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He worked at the British Museum as Keeper of Oriental Manuscripts and Books (circa 1899-1936) and taught at University College London and SOAS.

Lionel Obadia is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology. He held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (circa 1946-1949), the State Council's translation administration department (circa 1952-1958), and the Ethnic Publishing House (circa 1958-1978).

Lisa Grumbach specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She has held academic posts at Stanford University and as an assistant professor (助教授) at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Walter M. Spink and earned her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, later holding a post at the University of North Texas in 2009.
Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the University of Oslo (2003-2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig and teacher Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Liu Zaifu was a Sinologist who studied at Xiamen University (circa 1959-1963). He held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences beginning in 1963 and at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology around 2000.

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He completed a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara by 1990 and became Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University circa 1993.
